tables.name: effects
tables.description: One effect row per Stripe, calendar or Linq contact call a commit (or a clock firing with no turn) causes: the call runs from this row, so a crash or retry never doubles or loses it (arch 10 line 508). One idempotency key over all its tries; 5 tries in 10 minutes, then that service's outage row; a card decline never retried (arch 10 line 542). Reconciliation matches Stripe charges and refunds to ledger lines by its id (arch 10 line 550). K-07's schema (effectRow) gives each column's meaning and the state moves.
tables.source: 02-contracts K-07 'Effect rows' and its schema addition (migrated with K-05 v1.1); arch 01 line 77; arch 05 line 267; arch 10 lines 508, 542, 550; arch 11 lines 572, 582; CQ-04

columns.name: id
columns.description: The effect id (CQ-09: an opaque string code makes); reconciliation matches by it.

columns.name: turn_id
columns.description: The turn whose commit wrote it (turns.id); null when a job wrote it.

columns.name: job_id
columns.description: The job that wrote it when no turn did, such as the minute sweep firing monthly billing (K-04 event_log.job_id).

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business it is for (businesses.id); null for a Linq contact, which belongs to Rosie's one number.

columns.name: booking_id
columns.description: The booking it is about (bookings.id), or null.

columns.name: kind
columns.description: K-07 effectKind: stripe_save_card, stripe_charge, stripe_refund, stripe_pay_link, stripe_dispute_evidence, rosfield_monthly_charge, calendar_write, calendar_update, calendar_delete, linq_contact_add.
columns.source: 02-contracts K-07; arch 01 line 77; arch 05 line 267; CQ-04

columns.name: port
columns.description: stripe, calendar or linq: the port it runs through (K-14, K-16, K-11).

columns.name: calendar_provider
columns.description: google or microsoft for a calendar effect; null otherwise.

columns.name: visit_id
columns.description: For a calendar effect, the visit (one event per visit and person); K-30 names the visit row, so no foreign key yet.

columns.name: person_id
columns.description: For a calendar effect, the booked person whose calendar holds the event; for a Stripe effect, the payer or the person refunded (persons.id).

columns.name: handle_id
columns.description: For linq_contact_add, the mobile's handle (handles.id).

columns.name: amount_cents
columns.description: For a charge, refund, pay link or monthly charge, the amount in whole cents.
columns.source: CQ-09 (money in integer cents with a currency code)

columns.name: currency
columns.description: The amount's currency code, three capital letters; set with amount_cents.

columns.name: port_request
columns.description: The request in the port's terms, as a JSON object; its shape is K-14's, K-16's or K-11's. Never a key or a card number.
columns.source: 02-contracts K-07 ('the request in the port's terms'); BP rule 7; arch 02 line 109

columns.name: idempotency_key
columns.description: One idempotency key over all its tries; unique.

columns.name: state
columns.description: K-07 effectState: pending, running, succeeded, declined, outage or cancelled.
columns.source: 02-contracts K-07; arch 10 line 542; arch 11 line 582; S12-16 to S12-18

columns.name: tries
columns.description: Tries in the current run, 0 to 5.

columns.name: runs
columns.description: Runs: 1, then 1 more each time it runs again after its service's outage.
columns.source: arch 11 line 582 ('Charges and refunds wait, then run once')

columns.name: first_try_at
columns.description: When the current run's first try went; the 10 minutes count from it.

columns.name: last_try_at
columns.description: When the latest try went.

columns.name: claimed_by
columns.description: The effects runner instance holding it while running; null otherwise.
columns.source: 02-contracts K-05 v1.1 (claim effect rows); README 'How a claim lapses'

columns.name: claim_lapses_at
columns.description: When the runner's claim lapses unless renewed, so a runner that died never strands it.

columns.name: provider_object_id
columns.description: The provider's id of what it made or changed (a charge, refund, pay link, calendar event or contact).
columns.source: 02-contracts K-07 ('the state, tries and provider ids')

columns.name: error_code
columns.description: The last error the provider or the network gave.

columns.name: ledger_line_id
columns.description: The ledger line it writes or matches; K-28 names the ledger, so no foreign key yet.

columns.name: trace_id
columns.description: Its trace id.

columns.name: created_at
columns.description: When it was written; reconciliation reads the last 48 hours (arch 10 line 550).

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one; a claim and a result compare and set it.
columns.source: arch 01 line 85; arch 10 line 506; K-04 v1 rule 2

checks.name: effects_port_matches_kind
checks.expression: (port = 'stripe' and (kind like 'stripe\_%' or kind = 'rosfield_monthly_charge')) or (port = 'calendar' and kind like 'calendar\_%') or (port = 'linq' and kind = 'linq_contact_add')

checks.name: effects_calendar_keyed
checks.expression: (port <> 'calendar' or (calendar_provider in ('google', 'microsoft') and booking_id is not null and visit_id is not null and person_id is not null)) and (port = 'calendar' or (calendar_provider is null and visit_id is null))
checks.source: arch 05 line 267 (keyed by booking id, visit and person); MC 8 'Calendars'

checks.name: effects_money_kinds_have_amount
checks.expression: (kind not in ('stripe_charge', 'stripe_refund', 'stripe_pay_link', 'rosfield_monthly_charge') or amount_cents is not null) and (amount_cents is null) = (currency is null) and (currency is null or currency ~ '^[A-Z]{3}$')

checks.name: effects_running_is_claimed
checks.expression: (state = 'running') = (claimed_by is not null and claim_lapses_at is not null)

indexes.name: effects_claimable_idx
indexes.why: The effects runner claims pending rows, and running rows whose claim lapsed, oldest first (K-05 v1.1 claim effect rows).

indexes.name: effects_outage_idx
indexes.why: When a service is back, its waiting effects run once, oldest first (arch 11 line 582).

indexes.name: effects_calendar_event_idx
indexes.why: A move or call-off finds the visit's event for that person (arch 05 line 267).

indexes.name: effects_turn_idx
indexes.why: A turn's effects, for replay and the console (arch 10 line 508).

indexes.name: effects_reconcile_idx
indexes.why: Daily reconciliation over the last 48 hours (arch 10 line 550).

tables.name: provider_events
tables.description: Stripe and calendar events, stored once by their event id after the gateway verifies them, and linked to their effect rows (arch 02 line 109: 'Stripe and calendar events go to PostgreSQL'). A known event id is dropped (200).
tables.source: 02-contracts K-07 'Provider events' and its schema addition; arch 02 line 109; arch 11 lines 578 to 582

columns.name: provider
columns.description: stripe, google_calendar or microsoft_calendar.

columns.name: provider_event_id
columns.description: The provider's event id: with provider, the key it is stored once by.

columns.name: event_type
columns.description: The provider's own name for the event (K-14, K-16 name the list).

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.description: When the provider says it happened, if it says.

columns.name: received_at
columns.description: When the gateway received it.

columns.name: business_id
columns.description: The business it concerns (businesses.id), when known.

columns.name: effect_id
columns.description: The effect row it reports on (effects.id), or null.

columns.name: payload
columns.description: The event's fields as the port parses them; never a key or a card number.

columns.name: trace_id
columns.description: The trace opened at receipt.

columns.name: handled_at
columns.description: When the runtime acted on it (matched its effect, told the owner of a clash); null until then.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: handling it updates it once.

indexes.name: provider_events_effect_idx
indexes.why: An effect's events, for its result and reconciliation (arch 10 line 550).

indexes.name: provider_events_unhandled_idx
indexes.why: Events not yet acted on, oldest first.

tables.name: outbox_claims
tables.description: The claim on an outbox row in state sending: who holds it and when it lapses, so a dispatcher that died never strands its recipient's later rows (K-04 v1 has no claim-time column; K-05 v1 open gap 1). One row per outbox row, written at its first claim and updated at each re-claim.
tables.source: 02-contracts K-05 item 3 ('with a claim so no row is sent twice'); K-05 v1 open gap 1; arch 11 line 576; README 'How a claim lapses'

columns.name: outbox_row_id
columns.description: The claimed row (outbox_rows.id).

columns.name: claimer
columns.description: The dispatcher instance holding it (K-05 v1 claimOutbox claimer).

columns.name: claimed_at
columns.description: When this claim was taken.

columns.name: lapses_at
columns.description: When it lapses unless renewed (claimed_at plus 60 s, renewed by 60 s at each part attempt: README default 2).
columns.source: README 'How a claim lapses'; arch 01 line 61 (the 60 s turn lease it mirrors)

columns.name: claim_no
columns.description: 1 for the first claim, raised by each re-claim.

columns.name: version
columns.description: The row's version: a re-claim or a renewal compares and sets it.

indexes.name: outbox_claims_lapses_idx
indexes.why: The claim walk finds sending rows whose claim lapsed.

rowLevelSecurity.why: Written and read only by the dispatcher on the runtime side, never by a Tool API call, as K-04's outbox_parts.
